outcome: Neonatal oral bacteriome (alpha diversity, bacterial composition)
Neonatal fecal bacteriome (alpha diversity, bacterial composition, relative abundances of genera)
cohort: The study included 66 healthy mother-neonate pairs, with 33 exposed to IAP during C-section or vaginal delivery and 33 controls who had vaginal delivery without IAP.
finding: IAP was associated with decreased alpha diversity and altered bacterial composition in neonatal oral samples within 48 hours after birth, and also with decreased alpha diversity and altered relative abundances of genera (Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, Enterococcus, Rothia) in transitional stool samples.
cross-section timing: Within 48 hours after birth for oral samples; meconium and transitional stool samples collected during hospital stay in the first week of life.
